chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Qunut, so he said: 'In what is recited aloud.' I said to him, 'I asked your father about that, and he said: 'In all five [prayers].' He said: 'May Allah have mercy on my father. The companions of my father came to him and asked him, so he informed them with the truth. Then they came to me as doubtful, so I issued a fatwa to them with taqiyyah (dissimulation).'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْقُنُوتِ: Qunut (supplication recited in the final rak'ah of Fajr prayer)

ai.seo_question: When should the Qunut be recited aloud during the five daily prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Qunut is recited aloud in all five daily prayers, revealing that his father’s previous instruction to recite it quietly was a case of *taqiyyah* (dissimulation) to prevent confusion among companions who had not yet received the definitive ruling. This narration highlights the dynamic nature of jurisprudential guidance in Shia tradition, where the Imam may conceal the full truth temporarily for the benefit of the community's understanding or to avoid fitna. It underscores the importance of distinguishing between the actual ruling (*al-haqq*) and the reported ruling due to dissimulation (*al-taqiyyah*).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Qunut, so heasws said: ‘In what you have to be loud with the recitation’. So I said, ‘I asked yourasws fatherasws about that, so heasws said: ‘In the five (Obligatory) Salāt, all of them’. So heasws said: ‘May Allahazwj have Mercy on myasws fatherasws. The companions of myasws fatherasws came to himasws and asked himasws, so heasws informed them with the truth. Then they come to measws as doubtful, so Iasws issued a Fatwa to them with ‘بِالتَّقِيَّةِ’ the dissimulation’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from abu Basir who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Qunut (supplication after recitation in second Rak‘at). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is in Salah (prayer) in which recitation is loudly?’ I (the narrator) then said to him (the Imam), ‘I asked your father about it and he said that it is in all of the five daily Salah (prayer).’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘I pray to Allah to grant favors to my father, the companions of my father asked him and he informed them of the truth. Thereafter skeptics came to me and I made a presentation according to Taqiyah.’”
